content_html:
Industrial Heat Exchangers: Shell and Tube & Finned Coil

We build two families of heat exchanger. Shell and tube units move heat between two process fluids and are the standard choice for high pressure, high temperature and fouling duties. Finned-coil units reject heat straight to the air, cooling or heating a fluid where cooling water is scarce or unwanted. Both are built to your process data and site conditions.

Shell and Tube Heat Exchangers

  • Fixed tubesheet: simplest and lowest cost, for clean services where the shell side needs no mechanical cleaning.
  • U-tube: the bundle expands freely and can be pulled for shell-side cleaning, with the tube side limited to chemical cleaning.
  • Floating head: bundle removable for cleaning on both sides, for dirty services and wide temperature differences.
  • Thermal and mechanical design to TEMA classes R, C or B and recognized pressure vessel codes, with baffle layout balanced against pressure drop and vibration.

Finned-Coil Heat Exchangers

  • Air-cooled coolers: process fluid in finned tubes with fans moving ambient air across the coil. No cooling water, no cooling tower and no water treatment.
  • Air heaters and coolers: steam, hot water or chilled water coils for heating or cooling process air, dryers and ventilation.
  • Radiators and dry coolers: closed-loop cooling of engine jacket water, glycol and compressor circuits.
  • Fin type, fin pitch, tube rows and circuiting chosen for the duty, the air side pressure drop and how dirty the air is.

Choosing Between Them

Shell and tube suits liquid-to-liquid and steam duties, high pressures and fluids that foul. Finned coil suits sites where cooling water is limited or expensive, and duties where the fluid can be cooled to within 10–15 °C of ambient air. Send your process data and we will recommend the type.

Service and Retubing

Tube leaks, fouling, fin damage and corrosion are the usual end of a bundle or coil. We offer heat exchanger repair, retubing, coil cleaning and bundle replacement, so a failing exchanger can be renewed to its original footprint.

Key Features and Benefits

  • Fixed, U-tube and floating head bundles for different cleaning needs
  • Air-cooled coils that remove the need for cooling water
  • Wide choice of tube, fin and shell materials for corrosive services
  • Replacement bundles and coils matched to existing nozzles and frames
  • Hydrostatic test and inspection documentation on request
